body.p: Claims 21, 23-27, 29, 31-37, and 39-50 are pending. Claims 1-20, 22, 28, 30, and 38 were previously cancelled. Claim 27 has been cancelled without prejudice to, or disclaimer of, the underlying subject matter. Claim 21 have been amended without prejudice to, or disclaimer of, the underlying subject matter. Support for the amendments may be found in the original claims and specification, e.g., at paragraph [0103] and Table 1. No new matter enters by way of the present amendments. Reconsideration of the application based on the above amendments and following remarks is respectfully requested.
Claims 21, 23-26, 29, and 37 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as allegedly being

unpatentable over U.S. 2016/0338591 to Lachenbruch et al. ("Lachenbruch") in view of U.S. 2015/0186607 to Geleijnse et al. ("Geleijnse"), further in view of "Capacitive Biosensors" to Berggren et al. ("Berggren"). See Office Action at 6. Claim 27 is further rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren as applied to claim 21, and further in view of U.S. Patent No. 9,028,407 to Bennet-Guerrero ("Bennet-Guerrero"). See Id. at 15.
Applicant respectfully disagrees.
At the outset, without acquiescing to the rejection, and solely to advance prosecution,
claim 21 has been amended to recite the features of claim 27. To the extent the Examiner applies the rejection of claim 27 to amended claim 21, Applicant submits the following arguments.

Regarding claim 27, the Examiner alleges that Bennet-Guerrero provides "continuing to make a plurality of measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-K if the delta value does not exceed the threshold, and making a plurality of measurements at a pre- determined frequency corresponding to level-N if the delta value exceeds the threshold." Id. at 15. As such, the Examiner concludes that "[o]ne of ordinary skill at the time [] the invention was filed would have found it obvious to continue to make a plurality of measurements at a pre-

determined frequency corresponding to level-K if the delta value does not exceed the threshold, and making a plurality of measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-N if the delta value exceeds the threshold as taught by Bennett-Guerrero in the method as taught by Lachenbruch et al., Geleijnse et al., and Berggren in combination with the motivation(s) of being a way to store and retrieve information from a database." Id. at 15-16. Applicant respectfully disagrees.

Applicant respectfully submits that aprimafacie case of obviousness has not been established for amended claim 21 for at least the following two reasons: (a) Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, Berggren, and Bennett-Guerrero, alone or in combination, do not provide or suggest each and every element of amended claim 21 and (b) a person of ordinary skill in the art combining the cited references would not have arrived at the claimed subject matter with a reasonable expectation of success.
(a) Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, Berggren, and Bennett-Guerrero, alone or in
combination, do not provide or suggest each and every element of amended claim 21
Applicant respectfully submits that Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, Berggren, and Bennett- Guerrero, alone or in combination, do not provide or suggest each and every element of amended claim 21.
It is well-established law for an obviousness rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 103 that the
references, either alone or combined, must provide all of the elements of the claim. The Office is required to make "a searching comparison of the claimed invention - including all its limitations

- with the teaching of the prior art." In re Ochiai, 71 F.3d 1565, 1572 (Fed. Cir. 1995), and CFMT v. Yieldup Intern. Corp., 349 F.3d 1333, 1342 (Fed. Cir. 2003). When "[t]he prior art reference (or references when combined) [do] not teach or suggest all the claim limitations, ... [o]ffice personnel must explain why the difference(s) between the prior art and
the claimed invention would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art." M.P.E.P. at

The Examiner has not at least shown that the cited references, alone or in combination, provide or suggest "calculating a delta value by a difference between two of the plurality of SEM measurements, determining whether the delta value exceeds a threshold, continuing to administer the current PU intervention and make a plurality of SEM measurements at a pre- determined frequency corresponding to level-K if the delta value does not exceed the threshold, and administering a new PU intervention of level-N and making a plurality of SEM measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-N if the delta value exceeds the threshold, where N has a value greater than K." as is recited in amended claim 21.

The Examiner acknowledges that Lachenbruch, Geleijnse and Berggren "in combination may not specifically, further teach ... making a plurality of measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-N if the delta value does not exceed the threshold and making a plurality of measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-K if the delta value exceeds the threshold." Office Action at p. 16.
Indeed, Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, and Berggren, alone or in combination, are silent

regarding making a plurality of measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-N if the delta value does not exceed the threshold and making a plurality of measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-K if the delta value exceeds the threshold as is recited in amended claim 21.

The Examiner goes on to cite Bennet-Guerrero et al, alleging that "column 6, lines 16-21 of Bennet-Guerrero" remedies the deficiencies of Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, and Berggren. Id. at p. 17. Applicant respectfully disagrees. Applicant respectfully submits that Bennet-Guerrero, at best, provides a protocol for measuring the chest incline angle of a subject every one minute to "less frequently, such as only once every ten minutes, which may be beneficial for various reasons, such as to enhance, improve, or even optimize battery life." Bennet-Guerrero at column
6 lines 19-21.
First, a person of ordinary skill in the art reading Bennet-Guerrero as a whole would

understand that Bennet-Guerrero's disclosure recites measuring an incline position of a subject, which is different than Applicant's disclosure addressing "a clear need to identify tissue damage earlier so that interventions can prevent progression of the subepidermal damage to stage-1 and beyond." Specification at [0154]. Second, Applicant's disclosure indicates that different risk levels and their recommended interventions may require a different frequency of monitoring, for example as is described in Table 1. In contrast, Bennet-Guerrero is silent as to "continuing to... make a plurality of SEM measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-K if the delta value does not exceed the threshold." Rather, Bennet-Guerrero recites "if data is obtained that indicates a decreased risk of occurrence of an unwanted or dangerous condition, the then chest incline can be measured relatively less frequently. This operation may be beneficial for other reasons, such as to conserve battery life or increase longevity of the senor or sensor system." See Benet-Guerrero at column 6 lines 43-49.

For at least the above reasons, Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, Berggren, and Bennet-Guerrero, alone or in combination, do not provide or suggest each and every element of amended claim 21. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that the amended claim 21 is nonobvious over Lachenbruch, in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren and Bennet-Guerrero.
(b) A person of ordinary skill in the art combining the cited references would not have arrived at the claimed subject matter with a reasonable expectation of success

Notwithstanding that Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, Berggren and Bennet-Guerrero, alone or in combination, do not provide or suggest all the elements of amended claim 21, the Examiner alleges that there is motivation of "being beneficial for various reasons such as to enhance, improve, or even optimize battery life." Office Action at 17. Applicant respectfully disagrees.
To establish aprimafacie case of obviousness, there must be some suggestion or

motivation, either in the references themselves or in the knowledge generally available to one of skill in the art, to modify the reference or to combine reference teachings. See M.P.E.P §2143.01 There must also be a reasonable expectation of success. See M.P.E.P §2143.02

One of ordinary skill in the art combining Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, Berggren and Bennet- Guerrero would not have arrived at the claimed subject matter of amended claim 27 with a reasonable expectation of success. As previously discussed in Section (a), Bennet-Guerrero provides a frequency of measurement of an incline angle of a subject's chest and reducing the frequency to conserve battery life, whereas claim 21 as amended requires "continuing...to make a plurality of SEM measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-K" or "making a plurality of SEM measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level- K" according to the recited delta value. Accordingly, one of ordinary skill in the art would understand that Bennet-Guerrero's disclosure of reducing measurement frequency is not a basis for predicting success of the claimed method steps of amended claim 21. Hence, there would not be a reasonable expectation of success to apply an element of Bennet-Guerrero's protocol for reducing measurement frequency, much less a modified version of such a protocol, to Applicant's protocol to achieve an alleged comparable result.

For at least the above reasons, Applicant respectfully submits that amended claim 21 is nonobvious over Lachenbruch, in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren and Bennet- Guerrero. Because dependent claims 23-26, 27, 29, and 37 recite all the elements of claim 21, these dependent claims also are non-obvious over Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, Berggren and Bennet- Guerrero. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner withdraw the rejection of claims 21, 23-26, 27, 29, and 37 under 35 U.S.C. §103 over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren.
B. Claims 31, 32, 34, and 39

unpatentable over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren as applied to claim 29, and further in view of U.S. Patent No. 9,675,289 to Heaton ("Heaton"). See Office Action at 17. Specifically for claim 31, the Examiner alleges that Heaton provides "querying the database for data to form retrieved data values (see FIG. 9 where there is a directory for storing and retrieving archived responses into and from the database. In order for the system here to

access the database here, it would query the database in order to retrieve the necessary data)." Id. at 16. As such, the Examiner concludes that "[o]ne of ordinary skill at the time the invention was filed would have found it obvious to query the database for data to form retrieved delta values as taught by Heaton in the method as taught by Lachenbruch et al., Geleijnse et al., and Berggren in combination with the motivation(s) of being a way to store and retrieve information from a database." Id. at 17. Applicant respectfully disagrees.

If an independent claim is nonobvious under 35 U.S.C. 103, then any claim depending therefrom is nonobvious. In re Fine, 837 F.2d 1071 (Fed. Cir. 1988). Claims 31, 32, 34, and 39 are dependent directly or indirectly from claim 21, and incorporates the features of claim 21. Since the Examiner has not shown that amended claim 21 is obvious in view of Lachenbruch, Geleijnse, Berggren, and Brem, and Heaton does not remedy the deficiencies of these references as discussed in Section A above, claims 31, 32, 34, and 39 are also nonobvious.
For at least the above reasons, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner

withdraw the rejection of claims 31-32, 34, and 39 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Lachenbruch in view of Geleijnse, further in view of Berggren and Brem as previously applied to claim 29, and further in view of Heaton.
